title: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026 — Rare Earths
date_evidence: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, February 2026
key_claim: Rare earths were mined and processed domestically in 2025 (51,000 tons of REO concentrate; 8,900 tons of compounds and metals), but U.S. imports of rare-earth compounds and metals increased 169% in 2025 and net import reliance rose to 67% of apparent consumption (from 53% in 2024); import sources for 2021-24 were China 71%, Malaysia 13%, Japan 5% and Estonia 5%; in April 2025 China tightened export controls on seven heavy rare earths, expanded them in October 2025, then suspended the October controls for one year in November while the April controls remained in effect.
notes: Tier 1 primary government data. Structural anchor (3-6m band, Feb 2026): the canonical U.S. import-reliance dataset that grounds the dependency framing. Cited inline like any other source. Read from the USGS MCS2026 rare-earths chapter PDF.

title: MP Materials Reports First Quarter 2026 Results (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)
date_evidence: LAS VEGAS, May 7, 2026 - MP Materials Corp. (NYSE: MP) ... today announced financial and operational results for the three months ended March 31, 2026.
key_claim: MP Materials describes itself as America's only fully integrated rare earth producer, with capabilities spanning mining, processing, metallization and magnet manufacturing; in Q1 2026 it reported record NdPr production of 917 metric tons (up 63% year over year) and record NdPr sales of 1,006 metric tons (up 117%), $42.3 million of price-protection-agreement income, the start of scaled heavy rare earth separation commissioning at Mountain Pass, the groundbreaking of its 10X magnetics facility, and ongoing NdFeB magnet manufacturing begun in December 2025 under transactions with the U.S. Department of War (formerly Department of Defense) and a long-term Apple agreement.
verbatim_quote: America's only fully integrated rare earth producer
notes: Tier 1 primary SEC filing. Evidence that the leading U.S. integrated producer is ramping midstream/magnet capacity but from a low base, supported by a government price floor (PPA income). Read from SEC EDGAR.

title: USA Rare Earth Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1)
date_evidence: STILLWATER, Okla. - May 13, 2026 - USA Rare Earth, Inc. (Nasdaq: USAR) ... announced its financial and operational results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026.
key_claim: USA Rare Earth is building a fully integrated rare earth and permanent magnet value chain across the United States, United Kingdom, France and Brazil; it announced a ~$2.8 billion definitive agreement to acquire Serra Verde, described as the only large-scale producer of vital heavy rare earths outside Asia, de-risked with a 15-year 100% offtake agreement including price floors; it completed the first commercial yttrium metal production outside China at its UK facility in April 2026; it expects a $1.6 billion Department of Commerce CHIPS Program funding package; and it commissioned Phase 1a of its Stillwater NdFeB magnet facility, ramping toward 600 MTPA by Q4 2026.
verbatim_quote: the only large-scale producer of vital HREEs outside Asia
notes: Tier 1 primary SEC filing. Evidence of the most ambitious Western mine-to-magnet build-out and its reliance on price-floor offtake and government funding. Read from SEC EDGAR.

publisher: CSIS (Center for Strategic and International Studies)
title: Rare Earth Export Restrictions One Year Later
date_evidence: By Gracelin Baskaran and Meredith Schwartz APRIL 2026 ... Rare Earth Export Restrictions One Year Later (file path 2026-04/260427)
key_claim: China's October 2025 expansion added a strict foreign direct product rule and an embargo on the outflow of skilled Chinese nationals and proprietary technology to foreign projects before the controls were suspended for one year; the United States has mobilised over $7.3 billion in capital across five agencies, $110 per kilogram price floors, guaranteed government offtake, Project Vault and bilateral frameworks (Australia, Japan, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia), yet China continues to dominate processing, refining and downstream manufacturing; Chinese yttrium exports to the United States fell to 17 tons in the eight months after the April 2025 controls from 333 tons before; the DOD bars Chinese, Russian, Iranian and North Korean rare earth magnets from January 1, 2027; and despite the distance travelled, displacement measured in actual output remains modest with self-sufficiency a long road, as solvent-extraction separation of chemically similar heavy rare earths remains the hardest, China-dominated step.
verbatim_quote: an embargo on the outflow of skilled Chinese nationals and proprietary technology to foreign projects
notes: Tier 2 think-tank brief by the director of CSIS's Critical Minerals Security Program. Primary anchor for the technology/know-how-control thesis, the U.S. policy response, and the sourced counter-evidence (exports resumed but displacement modest). Read from the CSIS PDF.

publisher: CSIS (Center for Strategic and International Studies)
title: Developing Rare Earth Processing Hubs: An Analytical Approach
date_evidence: CSIS, 'Developing Rare Earth Processing Hubs: An Analytical Approach', by Meredith Schwartz and Gracelin Baskaran, published April 15, 2026.
key_claim: The midstream — separation, refining and metallization capacity — remains the single greatest bottleneck in the Western rare earth supply chain; without it, upstream discoveries and downstream ambitions cannot connect, and the United States must develop a strategy to rebuild rare earth technical expertise and establish midstream processing hubs beyond China's control.
verbatim_quote: the single greatest bottleneck in the Western supply chain
notes: Tier 2 think-tank analysis (CSIS Critical Minerals Security Program). Directly states the midstream-as-bottleneck thesis. Page is JS-heavy and exceeded fetch limits; date and thesis captured via WebSearch of the publisher and exact title and corroborated by the companion CSIS brief.

title: Beijing's dominance in rare earth processing leaves others scrambling to close the gap
key_claim: China accounts for roughly 70% of global rare earth production but close to 90% of the world's rare earth refining and processing capacity, the dominance that gives Beijing real leverage; separating heavy rare earths to magnet-grade purity is a slow, chemically delicate process that depends on specialized technology China currently controls, and mining executives say it could optimistically take a decade for other nations to build their own rare earth industry; the EU's 2024 Critical Raw Materials Act set 2030 benchmarks of 40% domestic processing and 25% recycling, and in October 2025 the US signed an $8.5 billion rare earth pact with Australia.
verbatim_quote: China is the leader, and the U.S. is far behind
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism. Quantification source for the mining-vs-processing share gap (~70% vs ~90%) and the specialized-technology dependency. Read from the page.

title: China Rare Earth Export Controls: April Curbs Still Bite After Beijing Summit
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-05-26T08:03:09-04:00 ; visible byline: Published: May 26 2026, 08:03 AM EDT
key_claim: China's April 2025 controls on seven heavy rare earth elements (MOFCOM Announcement No. 18) were never suspended and still require case-by-case approval for every shipment, while the more sweeping October 2025 controls — including extraterritorial provisions requiring a MOFCOM licence for any product made outside China that incorporates Chinese-origin rare earth materials or was produced using Chinese rare earth technologies — are suspended only until November 10, 2026; general licences issued to JL MAG, San Huan and Yunsheng from December 2025 ease civilian throughput but exclude defense and aerospace end-users; heavy rare earth exports run roughly 50% below pre-restriction levels; and the IEA's April 2026 report estimates up to $6.5 trillion in annual at-risk economic output outside China if the full suite of controls were reimplemented, with magnet rare earth demand projected to grow more than 30% by 2030.
verbatim_quote: produced using Chinese rare earth technologies
notes: Tier 3 trade/technology journalism. Source for the live regulatory structure (April controls intact, October controls suspended to Nov 2026, general-licence carve-outs) and the IEA $6.5tn risk figure. Used for both the recency hook and the Counter-Argument. Read from the page.
